newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast distillates edge higher, trade heavy.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast distillates edge higher, trade heavy.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot distillate prices added to early gains Tuesday afternoon, as futures prices helped spark active trade in the region, traders said.
"Compared to what (the market has) been in the last two to three weeks, its active," a trader said.
Upcoming refinery maintenance at refineries and increased exports sparked fears of near-term shortness, traders said.
Strength in crude futures also boosted West Coast markets, with January NYMEX adding 13 cents to yesterday's $1.05 rally. The contract settled at $24.93 a barrel.
Meanwhile, January heating oil finished 0.65 cents a gallon higher at 74.22 cents while gasoline jumped 1.01 cents on the day.
Los Angeles low sulphur diesle added another cent to early gains, trading late at 71/72 cents a gallon. A deal was heard done early at 70.50 cents.
Bids for jet feul rose 0.50 cents on rumors of increased exports, while CARB diesel rose as much 1.50 cents to 75/76 cents a gallon.
Bids for Los Angeles conventional unleaded gasoline flattned at 64.50 cents a gallon, with offers holding at 65 cents.
